repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
    wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == false)
    fired = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR specifies a rising-edge wait on MotionSensor.Motion, but the JoI uses a direct state check without edge detection. At 100ms, motion is already true (transitioned at 0ms), so the JoI's state check should fire but doesn't due to incorrect edge semantics. The IR's rising-edge wait requires tracking previous state to detect transitions, which the candidate lacks. F2 shows missing action at 100ms when IR fires.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replace the state-check-based if/else with the general repeating-edge state machine pattern: persist fired flag, wait for false edge, wait for true edge, execute body, mark fired. This preserves the IR's rising-edge semantics and cycle period of 1 SEC.
